pathway.title: VIASAT INC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months but does not solve the maturity wall. Cash plus undrawn revolvers of USD 2,886.12 million cover the current portion of debt 4.36 times, or 3.53 times without the Inmarsat revolving facility that expires 143 days after the as-of date, but the fiscal 2030 maturities equal 2.26 times last-twelve-month EBITDA and 96.46% of principal falls due within fiscal 2028 to fiscal 2031. The liquidity buys time to refinance rather than capacity to repay. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 173; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 37, 70; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C17

- Free cash flow is the weakest dimension. Operating cash flow less capital spending was USD 597.11 million in fiscal 2026 but USD 177.11 million without the Ligado lump sum, and USD 158.29 million over the last twelve months, which is 11.03% of EBITDA; total debt is 40.70 times that figure. The first quarter of fiscal 2027 produced USD 41.62 million against USD 60.45 million a year earlier. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110, 112, 130; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

- Leverage has improved less than the headline. Gross debt to EBITDA fell from 5.57x to 4.41x in fiscal 2026 and was 4.49x over the last twelve months, but 56.75% of the fall reflects the absence of a USD 169.4 million charge in the prior year, since fiscal 2025 leverage would have been 4.91x without it. Net debt to EBITDA was 3.28x, and every ratio rests on EBITDA built from statement lines because no filing defines an adjusted measure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 129, 137; calculation C8

- Interest cover is flattered by capitalization. EBITDA covers cash-paid interest 4.73x but incurred interest only 2.43x, and capitalized interest was 43.12% of incurred interest in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Capitalization ends on each satellite as it enters service, which raises expense and lowers reported cover, although seven satellites remain under construction and capitalized interest is part of the cost of those satellites, so free cash flow after capital spending is the cleaner test. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 98, 136; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 72; calculation C10; calculation C11

- The business profile is average: diversified by line, but growth has stalled before the satellite ramp and the largest line has no contracted minimums. Aviation services rose 13.66% in fiscal 2026 while fixed services fell 18.06% as bandwidth is rationed to aviation, last-twelve-month revenue is 0.31% below fiscal 2026 and first-quarter EBITDA fell 6.95% year on year. Recurring in-flight service contracts carry no minimum service purchase requirements, so they sit outside the USD 4.2 billion of remaining performance obligations, and capacity, not demand, is the stated constraint, which makes ViaSat-3 service the swing factor for revenue. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 106, 155; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C6; calculation C7

- Defense and advanced technologies is the earnings anchor. It earned 58.64% of fiscal 2026 segment operating profit on 28.89% of revenue and 44.42% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, with firm backlog up 15.65% in the quarter, but the U.S. Government was 16% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 18% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, and substantially all of its backlog can be terminated for convenience. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 53, 205; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 48, 68; calculation C14; calculation C15

- Refinancing capacity is average: market access has been shown, at a high price, and no rating or traded price is supplied. Inmarsat issued USD 1,975.0 million of 9.00% secured notes in September 2024 to redeem 6.75% notes, and the issuer's own fair value estimates at June 30, 2026 put the 2027 and 2028 notes at 99.73% and 99.75% of principal, the Inmarsat 2029 notes at 105.32% and the 2031 notes at 101.00%, all higher than at March 31, 2026, which is consistent with open access but is an estimate, not a quote. 38.70% of principal is floating-rate with no hedge described since the interest rate caps matured in February 2025, so a rise of 100 bp adds USD 25.42 million of annual interest. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 148, 181, 184; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 32, 78; calculation C9; calculation C23

- Financial policy and governance are average on observed behaviour: no dividend, falling principal and no sponsor, but the holder register, the cooperation agreement of May 6, 2026 and covenant levels are not supplied, so alignment is observed rather than assured. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: The first strength is liquidity: cash of USD 1,735.819 million and undrawn revolving capacity of USD 1,150.3 million at June 30, 2026 cover the current portion of debt 4.36 times, which lowers the probability of a liquidity event inside twelve months. The second is recurring aviation revenue, up 13.66% in fiscal 2026 on a growing installed aircraft base, which supports revenue visibility even though in-flight contracts carry no minimum purchase requirement. The third is the defense and advanced technologies segment, which earned 58.64% of segment operating profit and holds firm backlog of USD 1,401.6 million, supporting cash flow through a satellite ramp. The fourth is financial policy: no dividend, no buyback beyond tax withholding and principal down USD 619.16 million in fiscal 2026, which supports deleveraging. The fifth is firm backlog of USD 4,217.7 million, about half deliverable within twelve months, which supports near-term defense and fixed revenue though it excludes recurring in-flight revenue. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 37, 48, 68, 69, 70; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C18

The first weakness is thin free cash flow, USD 158.29 million over the last twelve months without the Ligado lump sum against capital spending of USD 1,013.689 million, which leaves debt dependent on EBITDA growth or asset sales to fall. The second is the maturity profile: 49.30% of principal falls due in fiscal 2030, the 2027 secured notes of USD 600.0 million are current and the Inmarsat revolving facility lapses on March 28, 2027, which makes refinancing the main test. The third is ViaSat-3 execution: the first satellite recovered less than 10% of its throughput, capacity has been constrained since fiscal 2023 and service starts are unconfirmed, which caps revenue growth and delays interest relief. The fourth is the interest burden: cover falls from 4.73x to 2.43x before capitalization and 38.70% of principal is floating-rate and unhedged, which raises sensitivity to rates and to the end of capitalization. The fifth is opaque ownership and covenant detail, which limits confidence in alignment and headroom. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 137, 148; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 38; calculation C1; calculation C9; calculation C11; calculation C13

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The defining transaction is the Inmarsat acquisition completed on May 30, 2023, in which Viasat bought all outstanding shares of Inmarsat Holdings for consideration transferred of USD 2,679.092 million, made up of USD 550.7 million of cash and Viasat shares valued at about USD 2.1 billion. Viasat assumed long-term debt of USD 3,519.774 million and recorded goodwill of USD 1,462.881 million and acquired intangible assets of USD 2,570.0 million. Two financings were arranged around the closing: a USD 616.7 million term loan in May 2023 and a USD 733.4 million unsecured bridge loan that the 2031 senior notes replaced in September 2023. The former Inmarsat owners received shares equal to about one third of today's share count, and their current holdings are not established. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 169, 175, 185; calculation C16

Inmarsat's own debt has been refinanced twice since closing. In March 2024 a USD 1.3 billion term loan and a USD 550.0 million revolving facility replaced most of the earlier term loan and the earlier USD 700.0 million revolver, and in September 2024 USD 1.975 billion of 9.00% secured notes due 2029 were issued to redeem the 6.75% secured notes due 2026, a coupon increase of 2.25 percentage points. In fiscal 2026 Viasat redeemed the remaining USD 442.6 million of its 2025 senior notes in May 2025, repaid USD 300.0 million of the original Inmarsat term loan in November 2025 and repaid the former export-credit loan at maturity on October 15, 2025. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 111, 176, 178, 180, 181, 184; calculation C26

The only new debt issue in the period is the export-credit facility of USD 188.7 million agreed on January 21, 2026 with the Export-Import Bank of the United States. It financed up to 85% of the launch and insurance costs of the first ViaSat-3 satellite (USD 175.8 million) plus USD 12.9 million of exposure fees, carries a fixed 4.78% rate (7.52% effective), is repayable in 16 semi-annual installments from May 2026 to a final maturity on November 25, 2033, is guaranteed by Viasat, Inc. and is secured by first-priority liens on the ViaSat-2 satellite and a pledge of the borrower's shares. The first installment reduced the balance to USD 176.934 million by June 30, 2026, and the financial covenants are a maximum total leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio whose levels are not printed. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 178, 179; 10-Q_2025-12-31_vsat-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 36; calculation C27

At June 30, 2026 total debt was USD 6,570.503 million: the Inmarsat group's term loan and 9.00% secured notes (USD 3,245.75 million), the Viasat group's two term loans, 2027 secured notes, 2028 and 2031 unsecured notes and export-credit facility (USD 3,182.075 million) and finance leases (USD 142.678 million). Both revolving facilities were undrawn: Viasat's USD 647.5 million facility had USD 47.2 million of letters of credit and USD 600.3 million available, and Inmarsat's USD 550.0 million facility, available in full, expires on March 28, 2027, 143 days after the as-of date. The 2027 secured notes of USD 600.0 million were classified as current at June 30, 2026, and the documents show no refinancing after August 6, 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 34, 37, 38; calculation C20; calculation C24

Other transactions shape the credit. The Link-16 tactical data link business was sold to L3Harris for about USD 1.96 billion in cash in January 2023; the energy services system integration business was divested in December 2024; Inmarsat's June 2025 settlement with Ligado Networks provides a USD 420.0 million lump sum received in October 2025, a USD 100 million payment due in March 2026 that remains outstanding pending resolution, and quarterly payments of about USD 16 million rising 3% a year through 2107; and Navarino UK was sold in March 2026 for USD 203.0 million with a gain of USD 168.1 million. TrellisWare declared a USD 155.7 million dividend in June 2025, of which USD 59.7 million went to minority holders in fiscal 2026. Events after March 31, 2026 are the launch of the third ViaSat-3 satellite in April 2026, the cooperation agreement of May 6, 2026 and the first export-credit installment in May 2026; the March 31, 2026 balance sheet reflects none of them. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110, 111, 133, 147, 203; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for VIASAT INC (Viasat, Inc., consolidated) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is audited fiscal 2026 and its comparatives, the quarter ended 2026-06-30 with its prior-year quarter, carrying-value debt, liquidity and the maturity ladder, all on the reported basis the filings support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage improved to 4.41x total debt to EBITDA at March 31, 2026 from 5.57x a year earlier, then edged up to 4.49x on a last-twelve-months basis at June 30, 2026, so deleveraging has paused while the 2027 secured notes move into current liabilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover improved to 4.73x on the same twelve months, but falls to 2.43x once interest capitalized on satellites under construction is counted, and EBITDA is built from statement lines because the issuer states none, so covenant measures may differ. Cash plus undrawn revolvers cover the current portion of debt 4.36 times, although the Inmarsat revolver expires within five months of the as-of date.

The quarterly report states no financing event after June 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage fell in fiscal 2026 for two reasons that deserve different weight. Carrying-value debt dropped from USD 7,036.109 million to USD 6,448.605 million as the 2025 notes were redeemed and the original Inmarsat term loan was repaid early, which is real deleveraging, but EBITDA also rose from USD 1,263.327 million to USD 1,462.590 million partly because the prior year carried USD 169.400 million of impairment and related charges from exiting EMEA locations. With that charge added back, an Analyst Judgement that is not applied to any ratio, fiscal 2025 leverage would be 4.91x rather than 5.57x, so the move to 4.41x overstates the underlying improvement. Over the last twelve months to June 30, 2026 leverage is 4.49x because EBITDA slipped to USD 1,435.586 million while debt stayed near USD 6,442.399 million, so further progress now depends on EBITDA growth as the ViaSat-3 satellites enter service or on repayment from cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage on cash interest paid rose from 3.24x in fiscal 2025 to 4.48x in fiscal 2026 and 4.73x over the last twelve months, helped by lower debt and by more interest being capitalized, but that cash measure is flattered by capitalization. The issuer capitalized USD 240.700 million of interest in fiscal 2026 against USD 215.400 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 62.400 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, and interest incurred before capitalization gives cover of only 2.43x in fiscal 2026 and 2.43x again over the last twelve months. Capitalization of a satellite's interest stops when it enters commercial service, as it did for the earlier ViaSat-2 satellite, and the filings expect the second and third ViaSat-3 class satellites to enter service in September 2026 and by late summer 2026, so interest expense and cash interest paid can rise without any new borrowing and the cash-paid cover is better read as a ceiling than a run rate.

fields.value: Operating cash flow of USD 1,589.885 million in fiscal 2026 includes the USD 420.0 million Ligado lump sum received in October 2025, of which USD 267.5 million was booked as deferred revenue and USD 152.5 million as interest income. After capital expenditure of USD 992.774 million, free cash flow was USD 597.111 million and falls to USD 177.111 million without the lump sum, an Analyst Judgement shown for comparison only. A further USD 100 million lump sum that was due in March 2026 remains outstanding pending resolution of certain matters, so the claim is unpaid rather than lost. In the quarter to June 30, 2026 free cash flow was USD 41.622 million against USD 60.447 million a year earlier, which is the cleaner read of underlying cash generation after interest and capital spending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at June 30, 2026 was USD 1,735.819 million of cash plus USD 1,150.3 million of undrawn revolver commitments net of standby letters of credit, USD 2,886.119 million in all, which covers the current portion of debt of USD 661.939 million, mostly the 2027 secured notes, 4.36 times. The Inmarsat revolver of USD 550.0 million expires on March 28, 2027, within five months of the as-of date, and the Viasat revolver carries a springing maturity ahead of certain material debt; without the Inmarsat facility liquidity is USD 2,336.119 million, still 3.53 times the current portion. The harder test lies later: by fiscal year the ladder runs USD 57.753 million, USD 655.322 million, USD 1,108.693 million, USD 3,246.671 million and USD 1,341.337 million for fiscal 2027 to 2031 and USD 175.339 million after, so the revolvers matter mainly as a bridge to refinancing the fiscal 2030 wall, and any extension of the Inmarsat facility after August 6, 2026 is not in the filings supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ratios rest on EBITDA derived from statement lines, because no filing supplied states EBITDA or an adjusted measure. The derived figure leaves impairment, disposal and acquisition charges in expense and adds back none of the USD 81.070 million of stock-based compensation in fiscal 2026, so it will differ from covenant and management definitions that are not available. Maximum leverage and minimum interest coverage tests apply to the Viasat revolver and the export credit facility, and a total net leverage and interest coverage test applies to the Inmarsat revolver, but no level is printed, so headroom cannot be judged; the issuer reports compliance at March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure add to the fixed obligations the cash flow must carry. Operating lease liabilities of USD 490.961 million are outside debt, while finance lease obligations of USD 138.952 million are inside it; purchase commitments including satellite-related agreements are USD 1,018.717 million within twelve months and USD 1,256.727 million after; satellite performance incentive obligations were USD 6.1 million at March 31, 2026 and USD 4.9 million at June 30, 2026; contract-audit reserves were USD 15.1 million at both dates; and a post-retirement medical plan assumed with Inmarsat is described without an amount. No pension, factoring, supplier-finance or securitization arrangement was found on search of the filings supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer advances and deferred revenue are a material non-interest-bearing funding source. Collections in excess of revenues plus the long-term portion of deferred revenues rose from USD 1,080.744 million at March 31, 2025 to USD 1,356.853 million at March 31, 2026 and USD 1,393.293 million at June 30, 2026, mainly because of the Ligado lump sum. This float supported fiscal 2026 operating cash flow and unwinds into revenue as obligations are performed, so revenue and EBITDA can include amounts for which no new cash arrives; creditors should watch whether operating cash flow after capital expenditure stays positive once the float stops growing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two events carry several figures that serve different purposes and are kept apart. The Ligado settlement expected USD 568 million in fiscal 2026, made up of the USD 420 million received, the USD 100 million unpaid and quarterly payments of about USD 16 million; the Navarino UK sale produced USD 203.0 million of proceeds in investing activities and a gain of USD 168.1 million in other income that sits outside EBITDA. No debt issue, repayment, acquisition, disposal or dividend dated after June 30, 2026 is stated, so no pro forma adjustment is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better credit view is liquidity of USD 2,886.119 million with both revolvers undrawn, reported covenant compliance at both balance-sheet dates, and firm backlog of USD 4,217.7 million at June 30, 2026. It would carry more weight if EBITDA recovers once the ViaSat-3 satellites are in service and the Inmarsat revolver is extended, and less if capitalized interest ends without matching EBITDA growth. A supported downside sequence starts with slow commercial ramp of the new satellites, after the reflector problem on the first ViaSat-3 satellite and a power anomaly on an Inmarsat satellite already led to a net loss of USD 905.496 million in fiscal 2024 after about USD 770.0 million of insurance claim receivables; EBITDA then stalls while interest stops being capitalized, cash interest rises, the 2027 secured notes and the Inmarsat revolver need refinancing, and leverage stays near its current level. Watch quarterly EBITDA, cash interest paid, the commercial start dates of the second and third satellites and any extension of the Inmarsat revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance analysis for VIASAT INC (the consolidated registrant Viasat, Inc.) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the group's transactions, ownership and control, business and operating model, governance and sponsor behaviour, read from the seven supplied documents through the quarter ended 2026-06-30 and the Source readiness analysis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Viasat is a listed, founder-led company with no sponsor or parent identified, no dividend and no documented extraction, so creditors face execution and refinancing risk more than owner risk, but ownership, board and covenant detail is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Communication services produced 71.11% of fiscal 2026 revenue of USD 4,640.3 million and defense and advanced technologies 28.89%. Aviation, at 25.68% of revenue, is the growth line while U.S. fixed broadband shrinks because satellite bandwidth is rationed in favour of aviation. The credit turns on the ViaSat-3 satellite ramp and the Inmarsat integration, and fiscal 2026 deleveraging coincided with non-recurring Ligado and Navarino receipts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 104, 106, 205; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control rests with a founder-led board and public holders, not a sponsor, but the holder register is not supplied, so concentration is not established. The founder has led the company since 1986, the board is classified with staggered three-year terms, blank-check preferred stock is authorised and action by written consent is barred, which slows any hostile change of control. A change of control lets noteholders put their notes at 101% and is an event of default under the secured credit facilities. About a third of today's shares were issued to Inmarsat's former owners in 2023, and an outside investor signed a cooperation agreement on May 6, 2026 whose terms are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy has been creditor-aligned so far: no dividend has been paid, buybacks are limited to shares withheld for employee taxes, and debt principal fell USD 619.16 million to USD 6.6 billion in fiscal 2026. The fall coincided with non-recurring receipts, a USD 420.0 million Ligado lump sum and USD 203.0 million from the Navarino sale, and the filings do not tie those receipts to the repayments, so a similar reduction is not assured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Growth and risk concentrate in aviation, although revenue is spread across several service and product lines. Aviation services rose 13.66% in fiscal 2026 and 10.75% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 while fixed services fell 18.06% and 27.08%, and installed commercial aircraft grew 9.46% on the approximate counts printed for the year to June 30, 2026. Recurring aviation revenue supports durability, but no airline customer or contract term is disclosed, so dependence on any one airline is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 106, 205; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 67; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Government exposure is material but not dominant. The U.S. Government was 16% of fiscal 2026 revenue, the five largest contracts about 19%, and substantially all U.S. Government backlog can be terminated for convenience. Defense and advanced technologies revenue grew 9.79% in fiscal 2026 and its firm backlog rose from USD 1,211.9 million at March 31, 2026 to USD 1,401.6 million at June 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 53, 107, 134; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 68; calculation C10; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Satellite execution is the central operating risk. The first ViaSat-3 satellite recovered less than 10% of its throughput after a reflector deployment failure, the company has been capacity constrained since fiscal 2023, and service on the second and third satellites was expected from September 2026 and by late summer 2026 with no document after August 6, 2026 to confirm either start. Insurance receivables of USD 770.0 million offset only part of the USD 1.67 billion write-down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fiscal 2026 cash flow overstates the run rate. Operating cash flow of USD 1.6 billion included the Ligado lump sum and capital spending absorbed USD 1.0 billion; with the lump sum removed, operating cash flow less capital spending was USD 177.11 million, assuming the whole lump sum sits in operating cash flow. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027 the same measure was USD 41.62 million against USD 60.45 million a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 113, 130; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C17; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The debt sits in two borrowing groups with no cross-guarantee stated. The Inmarsat group's term loan and 9.00% secured notes total USD 3,245.75 million on their own collateral, Viasat's secured term loans and 2027 notes share liens on substantially all of its assets, and the unsecured 2028 and 2031 notes of USD 1,133.4 million, 17.25% of principal, sit behind both. The 2027 secured notes are already classified as current and the Inmarsat revolving facility expires 143 days after the as-of date, and no document shows either refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 181, 182, 183, 184; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 34, 38; calculation C20; calculation C24; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure is adequate on statements but thin on creditor protections. No filing defines an adjusted EBITDA although executive awards are tied to Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and return on invested capital, and covenant levels, the proxy statement and the cooperation agreement are not supplied. Several senior roles changed between mid-2025 and April 2026, including the chief accounting officer in January 2026, which raises continuity risk during the satellite ramp.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a benign owner-risk view is what is missing rather than what is documented. The proxy statement is not supplied, a cooperation agreement with an outside investor dated May 6, 2026 is listed as a material contract, about a third of the share count was issued to former Inmarsat holders, and the Chairman and chief executive adopted a share-sale plan in March 2026 running to March 2027. Any of these could precede board change, buybacks or asset sales that favour shareholders over creditors. The company also admits it violated covenants in former revolving facilities and obtained waivers, with no date given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest operating case in favour is improving segment profitability: communication services segment operating profit rose from USD 40.9 million to USD 62.4 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, an 8% margin against 5%, and ViaSat-3 service would end the bandwidth rationing that is shrinking fixed broadband. A debt-funded distribution or buyback, a covenant waiver or amendment, board changes tied to the cooperation agreement, failure to extend or replace the Inmarsat revolving facility before March 28, 2027, delay or impairment of ViaSat-3 service, or failure to collect the USD 100 million Ligado payment still outstanding would move the view toward higher risk. Evidence of dispersed ownership, a refinanced revolver and ViaSat-3 service in commercial operation would move it toward lower risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, independence, pay and the holder register are not established; this limits the owner-risk conclusion to the absence of documented extraction, not proof of dispersed ownership.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The terms of the cooperation agreement dated May 6, 2026 are not supplied, so any board, standstill or strategy commitments are not established; this could reverse the finding that control sits with the board and public holders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Executed credit agreements and indentures are not supplied and covenant levels are printed in no filing, so capacity for dividends, investments and asset transfers is not established; the financial-policy conclusion rests on observed behaviour, not on what the documents permit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No document is dated after August 6, 2026, so the ViaSat-3 service starts, any Ligado resolution of the USD 100 million outstanding and any extension of the Inmarsat revolving facility are unconfirmed at the as-of date; the execution and refinancing conclusions may be out of date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Airline customers, contract lengths and renewal terms are not disclosed, and backlog excludes recurring in-flight connectivity revenue, so the durability of the aviation growth that drives the business view cannot be tested for single-customer dependence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management's own earnings framing is not supplied because the shareholder letters and slides behind the three results notices are absent, and no issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA exists in any filing; segment profit lines are the only earnings measure used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt is shown by borrower group from the notes, with no obligor-group statements, so the split of earnings and cash between the Viasat and Inmarsat groups is not established and structural subordination conclusions are qualitative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The defining transaction is the Inmarsat acquisition completed on May 30, 2023, in which Viasat bought all outstanding shares of Inmarsat Holdings for consideration transferred of USD 2,679.092 million, made up of USD 550.7 million of cash and Viasat shares valued at about USD 2.1 billion. Viasat assumed long-term debt of USD 3,519.774 million and recorded goodwill of USD 1,462.881 million and acquired intangible assets of USD 2,570.0 million. Two financings were arranged around the closing: a USD 616.7 million term loan in May 2023 and a USD 733.4 million unsecured bridge loan that the 2031 senior notes replaced in September 2023. The former Inmarsat owners received shares equal to about one third of today's share count, and their current holdings are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Inmarsat's own debt has been refinanced twice since closing. In March 2024 a USD 1.3 billion term loan and a USD 550.0 million revolving facility replaced most of the earlier term loan and the earlier USD 700.0 million revolver, and in September 2024 USD 1.975 billion of 9.00% secured notes due 2029 were issued to redeem the 6.75% secured notes due 2026, a coupon increase of 2.25 percentage points. In fiscal 2026 Viasat redeemed the remaining USD 442.6 million of its 2025 senior notes in May 2025, repaid USD 300.0 million of the original Inmarsat term loan in November 2025 and repaid the former export-credit loan at maturity on October 15, 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only new debt issue in the period is the export-credit facility of USD 188.7 million agreed on January 21, 2026 with the Export-Import Bank of the United States. It financed up to 85% of the launch and insurance costs of the first ViaSat-3 satellite (USD 175.8 million) plus USD 12.9 million of exposure fees, carries a fixed 4.78% rate (7.52% effective), is repayable in 16 semi-annual installments from May 2026 to a final maturity on November 25, 2033, is guaranteed by Viasat, Inc. and is secured by first-priority liens on the ViaSat-2 satellite and a pledge of the borrower's shares. The first installment reduced the balance to USD 176.934 million by June 30, 2026, and the financial covenants are a maximum total leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio whose levels are not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At June 30, 2026 total debt was USD 6,570.503 million: the Inmarsat group's term loan and 9.00% secured notes (USD 3,245.75 million), the Viasat group's two term loans, 2027 secured notes, 2028 and 2031 unsecured notes and export-credit facility (USD 3,182.075 million) and finance leases (USD 142.678 million). Both revolving facilities were undrawn: Viasat's USD 647.5 million facility had USD 47.2 million of letters of credit and USD 600.3 million available, and Inmarsat's USD 550.0 million facility, available in full, expires on March 28, 2027, 143 days after the as-of date. The 2027 secured notes of USD 600.0 million were classified as current at June 30, 2026, and the documents show no refinancing after August 6, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 34, 37, 38; calculation C20; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions shape the credit. The Link-16 tactical data link business was sold to L3Harris for about USD 1.96 billion in cash in January 2023; the energy services system integration business was divested in December 2024; Inmarsat's June 2025 settlement with Ligado Networks provides a USD 420.0 million lump sum received in October 2025, a USD 100 million payment due in March 2026 that remains outstanding pending resolution, and quarterly payments of about USD 16 million rising 3% a year through 2107; and Navarino UK was sold in March 2026 for USD 203.0 million with a gain of USD 168.1 million. TrellisWare declared a USD 155.7 million dividend in June 2025, of which USD 59.7 million went to minority holders in fiscal 2026. Events after March 31, 2026 are the launch of the third ViaSat-3 satellite in April 2026, the cooperation agreement of May 6, 2026 and the first export-credit installment in May 2026; the March 31, 2026 balance sheet reflects none of them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by undisclosed ownership, an unseen outside-investor agreement and undefined covenant capacity, because holders and documents that decide capital allocation are not visible, which implies refinancing and event risk that the documented absence of extraction does not remove. Countervailing evidence is no dividend, no sponsor fees and reduced principal in fiscal 2026. Module completed with limitations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for VIASAT INC (the consolidated registrant Viasat, Inc.) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated fundamental view built from Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance and checked against the supplied filings through the quarter ended 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Viasat is a leveraged satellite operator whose liquidity covers the next twelve months but whose free cash flow after interest and capital spending, without one-off receipts, is thin against USD 6.6 billion of debt, so creditors depend on ViaSat-3 service and on refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 114, 130; calculation C1; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross debt is 4.49x last-twelve-month EBITDA and net debt 3.28x, but EBITDA is derived from statement lines and the 4.73x cover on cash-paid interest falls to 2.43x before interest capitalized on satellites under construction. Liquidity is USD 2,886.12 million and the 2027 secured notes of USD 600.0 million are already current, yet 49.30% of principal falls due in fiscal 2030. The primary downside path is a slow ViaSat-3 ramp that stalls EBITDA while interest stops being capitalized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 38, 70; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months but does not solve the maturity wall. Cash plus undrawn revolvers of USD 2,886.12 million cover the current portion of debt 4.36 times, or 3.53 times without the Inmarsat revolving facility that expires 143 days after the as-of date, but the fiscal 2030 maturities equal 2.26 times last-twelve-month EBITDA and 96.46% of principal falls due within fiscal 2028 to fiscal 2031. The liquidity buys time to refinance rather than capacity to repay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 173; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 37, 70; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow is the weakest dimension. Operating cash flow less capital spending was USD 597.11 million in fiscal 2026 but USD 177.11 million without the Ligado lump sum, and USD 158.29 million over the last twelve months, which is 11.03% of EBITDA; total debt is 40.70 times that figure. The first quarter of fiscal 2027 produced USD 41.62 million against USD 60.45 million a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110, 112, 130; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage has improved less than the headline. Gross debt to EBITDA fell from 5.57x to 4.41x in fiscal 2026 and was 4.49x over the last twelve months, but 56.75% of the fall reflects the absence of a USD 169.4 million charge in the prior year, since fiscal 2025 leverage would have been 4.91x without it. Net debt to EBITDA was 3.28x, and every ratio rests on EBITDA built from statement lines because no filing defines an adjusted measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 129, 137; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest cover is flattered by capitalization. EBITDA covers cash-paid interest 4.73x but incurred interest only 2.43x, and capitalized interest was 43.12% of incurred interest in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Capitalization ends on each satellite as it enters service, which raises expense and lowers reported cover, although seven satellites remain under construction and capitalized interest is part of the cost of those satellites, so free cash flow after capital spending is the cleaner test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 98, 136; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 72; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business profile is average: diversified by line, but growth has stalled before the satellite ramp and the largest line has no contracted minimums. Aviation services rose 13.66% in fiscal 2026 while fixed services fell 18.06% as bandwidth is rationed to aviation, last-twelve-month revenue is 0.31% below fiscal 2026 and first-quarter EBITDA fell 6.95% year on year. Recurring in-flight service contracts carry no minimum service purchase requirements, so they sit outside the USD 4.2 billion of remaining performance obligations, and capacity, not demand, is the stated constraint, which makes ViaSat-3 service the swing factor for revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 106, 155; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Defense and advanced technologies is the earnings anchor. It earned 58.64% of fiscal 2026 segment operating profit on 28.89% of revenue and 44.42% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, with firm backlog up 15.65% in the quarter, but the U.S. Government was 16% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 18% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, and substantially all of its backlog can be terminated for convenience.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 53, 205; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 48, 68; calculation C14; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing capacity is average: market access has been shown, at a high price, and no rating or traded price is supplied. Inmarsat issued USD 1,975.0 million of 9.00% secured notes in September 2024 to redeem 6.75% notes, and the issuer's own fair value estimates at June 30, 2026 put the 2027 and 2028 notes at 99.73% and 99.75% of principal, the Inmarsat 2029 notes at 105.32% and the 2031 notes at 101.00%, all higher than at March 31, 2026, which is consistent with open access but is an estimate, not a quote. 38.70% of principal is floating-rate with no hedge described since the interest rate caps matured in February 2025, so a rise of 100 bp adds USD 25.42 million of annual interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 148, 181, 184; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 32, 78; calculation C9; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy and governance are average on observed behaviour: no dividend, falling principal and no sponsor, but the holder register, the cooperation agreement of May 6, 2026 and covenant levels are not supplied, so alignment is observed rather than assured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a thin-cash-flow view is operating momentum and a capital programme that is ending. Communication services segment operating profit rose 52.73% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 with the margin at 8% against 5%, aviation services grew 10.75%, management says capital spending may be flat to slightly down, firm backlog is USD 4,217.7 million, and Ligado still owes USD 100 million plus quarterly payments of about USD 16 million. If ViaSat-3 service adds revenue while capital spending falls, free cash flow without one-offs could rise well above USD 158.29 million, and the September 2024 refinancing suggests lenders will still lend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110, 113; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 67, 68; calculation C1; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Failure to start ViaSat-3 service on the dates expected, a further fall in first-quarter-style EBITDA, an unrefinanced 2027 secured note or Inmarsat revolving facility, or a debt-funded distribution would move the view toward higher risk; each 10% fall in last-twelve-month EBITDA lifts gross leverage from 4.49x to 4.99x. Free cash flow without one-offs above the level of the last twelve months, an extended Inmarsat revolver and service in commercial operation would move it toward lower risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No covenant level is printed for the maximum leverage and minimum cover tests on three facilities, so the liquidity and leverage conclusions cannot be tied to headroom and a covenant-driven acceleration cannot be ruled in or out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, traded price or spread is supplied and the issuer's fair value estimates of each note series are rounded model values, so refinancing capacity rests on past issuance and those estimates, not on current market access or cost, and the refinancing conclusion could be too benign if spreads have widened.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maintenance and growth capital spending are not split, so the capital programme's flexibility cannot be sized and the free cash flow conclusion assumes the indicated flat-to-slightly-down spending is achievable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contract lengths, churn and renewal terms are not disclosed and recurring in-flight contracts carry no minimum purchase requirement, so the revenue durability judgement rests on growth rates and installed base, not on contracted minimums.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest balance sheet is 128 days before the as-of date, so liquidity, the 2027 secured notes and the ViaSat-3 service starts may differ today and the near-term liquidity view is a snapshot.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings and cash cannot be split between the Viasat and Inmarsat borrowing groups, so each group's own ability to service its debt is not established and the combined ratios may hide a weaker group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is liquidity: cash of USD 1,735.819 million and undrawn revolving capacity of USD 1,150.3 million at June 30, 2026 cover the current portion of debt 4.36 times, which lowers the probability of a liquidity event inside twelve months. The second is recurring aviation revenue, up 13.66% in fiscal 2026 on a growing installed aircraft base, which supports revenue visibility even though in-flight contracts carry no minimum purchase requirement. The third is the defense and advanced technologies segment, which earned 58.64% of segment operating profit and holds firm backlog of USD 1,401.6 million, supporting cash flow through a satellite ramp. The fourth is financial policy: no dividend, no buyback beyond tax withholding and principal down USD 619.16 million in fiscal 2026, which supports deleveraging. The fifth is firm backlog of USD 4,217.7 million, about half deliverable within twelve months, which supports near-term defense and fixed revenue though it excludes recurring in-flight revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 37, 48, 68, 69, 70; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is thin free cash flow, USD 158.29 million over the last twelve months without the Ligado lump sum against capital spending of USD 1,013.689 million, which leaves debt dependent on EBITDA growth or asset sales to fall. The second is the maturity profile: 49.30% of principal falls due in fiscal 2030, the 2027 secured notes of USD 600.0 million are current and the Inmarsat revolving facility lapses on March 28, 2027, which makes refinancing the main test. The third is ViaSat-3 execution: the first satellite recovered less than 10% of its throughput, capacity has been constrained since fiscal 2023 and service starts are unconfirmed, which caps revenue growth and delays interest relief. The fourth is the interest burden: cover falls from 4.73x to 2.43x before capitalization and 38.70% of principal is floating-rate and unhedged, which raises sensitivity to rates and to the end of capitalization. The fifth is opaque ownership and covenant detail, which limits confidence in alignment and headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 137, 148; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 38; calculation C1; calculation C9; calculation C11; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Viasat sells connectivity services to airlines, ships, governments and fixed users, and defense, encryption and tactical networking products, through communication services (71.11% of fiscal 2026 revenue) and defense and advanced technologies (28.89%). Services were 70.57% of revenue, which gives recurring visibility, while almost all contracts are fixed-price, so cost overruns fall on Viasat. The May 2023 Inmarsat acquisition doubled the satellite and debt base and added L-band safety spectrum and customer relationships, and the group has since sold the Link-16 business, the energy services integration business and Navarino UK. These facts support cash-flow visibility in aviation and government satcom but raise debt service needs, so refinancing confidence depends on converting the satellite investment into EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 92, 169, 205; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Viasat is a listed, founder-led company with no sponsor or parent identified, so there is no sponsor behaviour to assess, and the filings document no dividend, no debt-funded distribution and a fall in principal. Debt sits in two groups: the Inmarsat group's term loan and 9.00% secured notes on their own collateral, and Viasat's secured term loans, 2027 secured notes and export-credit loan, with unsecured 2028 and 2031 notes ranking behind both and no subsidiary guaranteeing Viasat's debt at March 31, 2026. TrellisWare is majority-owned, so cash it distributes partly leaks to minority holders. The implication is that creditors rely on group-level cash flow, structural position by instrument and unseen holders' behaviour, all of which need the proxy statement, the executed documents and the cooperation agreement to confirm.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Volume drives revenue: installed commercial aircraft grew 9.46% year on year, while about 130,000 U.S. fixed subscribers at USD 113 per month became about 115,000 at USD 111 between March and June 2026, a fall of 11.54% in the count, because bandwidth is being allocated to aviation. Services were 70.57% of revenue and the U.S. Government 16%, with the five largest contracts about 19%; defense products are lumpy and depend on awards and government funding, and substantially all U.S. Government backlog can be terminated for convenience. Pricing power is not disclosed and contract lengths, churn and renewals are not stated; recurring in-flight service contracts carry no minimum service purchase requirements and are outside the USD 4.2 billion of remaining performance obligations, which refines the earlier finding that no airline contract term is disclosed. Revenue is therefore recurring and growing in aviation and government satcom, cyclical with airline traffic and defense budgets, concentrated at the top contracts, exposed to substitution by low earth orbit services such as Starlink, and structurally declining in U.S. fixed broadband, which limits cash-flow visibility to backlog and installed base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 20, 48, 53, 134, 155; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 53; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of service revenues was 46% of fiscal 2026 revenue, cost of product revenues 21%, selling, general and administrative 22%, independent research and development 4% and amortization of acquired intangibles 6%, with depreciation of USD 1,038.515 million equal to 22.38% of revenue, so the cost base is heavily fixed in satellites and ground networks. EBITDA margin was 31.52% in fiscal 2026 and 31.03% over the last twelve months; communication services segment margin improved from 5% to 8% in the first quarter while defense margin eased from 21% to 15% on a mix with less licensing revenue. Margins can be defended under modest volume pressure because management says capital spending may be flat to slightly down and selling cost fell, but fixed-price contracts, higher research spending (up 33% in the quarter) and fixed satellite depreciation leave little room if revenue stalls, so operating leverage cuts both ways.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-03-31_vsat-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 103, 113, 130, 206; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsat-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 66, 67, 68; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending was USD 992.774 million in fiscal 2026, 21.39% of revenue, and 21.91% over the last twelve months, against depreciation 1.05 times as large, so the asset base is being replaced rather than grown. EBITDA of USD 1,462.590 million converted to operating cash flow of USD 1,589.885 million only because of the Ligado lump sum; without it operating cash flow covers capital spending 1.16 times over the last twelve months. Cash interest paid was USD 326.548 million net of USD 240.7 million capitalized, cash taxes were USD 80.701 million, and deferred revenue rose USD 277.551 million in fiscal 2026, so reported cash flow includes funding that unwinds as revenue. Capital spending is committed for satellites under construction (USD 291.373 million of construction and related commitments) and capacity purchases of about USD 509.8 million, and management says fiscal 2027 spending may be flat to slightly down. EBITDA therefore turns into free cash flow of only about 11% once one-offs are excluded, which limits deleveraging and refinancing support.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and rising: the annual report names SpaceX, SES, Gogo, Panasonic Avionics, Anuvu, Iridium, Thales and Amazon Leo in aviation, which can force price or service concessions and shorten contract terms. New entrants are low earth orbit constellations, and the annual report says the geostationary industry is being disrupted by their adoption, which threatens renewals in aviation and maritime. Substitutes include air-to-ground and cellular services in fixed and mobility markets. Buyer power is high with airlines and governments, and the largest customer is the U.S. Government. Supplier power is moderate: components come from sole-source or limited suppliers and capacity is bought from third parties, which exposes delivery and cost. The credit implication is that margin durability and retention depend on ViaSat-3 capacity delivering cost per bit and on L-band safety services that LEO does not replace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation is material because authorizations to operate satellites and earth stations are conditional on milestones and fees, and loss or delay could stop service, while export controls, sanctions and U.S. Government contract audit rules apply; this bears on revenue and on orbital and spectrum assets recorded at USD 1,080.0 million in the Inmarsat purchase accounting. Economic factors matter through airline traffic and defense budgets, and 31.88% of revenue is from non-U.S. customers though business is generally conducted in U.S. dollars. Interest rates matter because 38.70% of principal is floating. Social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the materials supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are liquidity of USD 2,886.12 million, growing recurring aviation revenue, a profitable defense segment, a deleveraging record with no dividend and an owned multi-band fleet. Weaknesses are thin free cash flow, 4.49x gross leverage on unadjusted EBITDA, a concentrated maturity profile, floating-rate exposure and unseen covenants. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are ViaSat-3 service raising revenue per unit of capital, lower capital spending as satellites are completed, collection of the Ligado USD 100 million and its quarterly payments, and an extended revolver. Threats that could weaken it are service delay or impairment, low earth orbit competition at renewals, termination of U.S. Government backlog, higher rates and interest ceasing to be capitalized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are liquidity, a diversified recurring revenue base, a profitable defense segment and creditor-aligned financial policy; the main constraints are free cash flow after capital spending and the concentrated maturity profile. The trend is stable to slightly weaker: fiscal 2026 EBITDA margin 31.52% and gross leverage 4.41x improved on the prior year partly because a charge dropped out, while the last twelve months show EBITDA 1.85% lower and leverage 4.49x. Scale and market position are average to strong, competitive advantage average given low earth orbit disruption and L-band safety spectrum, diversification average, cost and capex flexibility average, margin stability average, free cash flow stability weak, refinancing access average, liquidity strong over twelve months and financial policy average. Key missing datapoints are covenant levels, ratings, an issuer adjusted EBITDA, capital spending split and obligor-group figures. Financial profile detail is partly qualitative where those datapoints are absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months the commercial start of ViaSat-3 service on the second and third satellites, lower capital spending, a lower interest burden from repaid debt and any extension of the Inmarsat revolving facility are the main tailwinds; the 2027 secured notes, the revolver expiry, the end of interest capitalization on satellites entering service and the loss of one-off Ligado and Navarino receipts are headwinds that pressure free cash flow and refinancing. Over three to five years the tailwinds are growth in aircraft and vessels needing connectivity, government demand for resilient communications and seven further satellites completing, while the headwinds are the fiscal 2030 maturities, low earth orbit competition at contract renewals and further satellite capital needs. Sector headwinds are the LEO disruption and tariffs affecting supply; sector tailwinds are rising connectivity demand. Company tailwinds are firm backlog and the Ligado stream of about USD 16 million a quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating event is a slower or weaker ViaSat-3 ramp, possible given that the first satellite recovered less than 10% of its throughput and that service starts are unconfirmed after August 6, 2026. The first operational break is that capacity stays rationed, so fixed services keep shrinking (down 27.08% in the first quarter) and aviation growth slows. Revenue and EBITDA stall near last-twelve-month levels while interest on satellites entering service stops being capitalized, so reported cover falls toward 2.43x; each 10% fall in EBITDA lifts gross leverage to 4.99x. Free cash flow without one-offs stays near USD 158.29 million, so the USD 600.0 million of 2027 secured notes and the Inmarsat revolver must be refinanced rather than repaid. Management levers are capital spending cuts, disposals such as Navarino, TrellisWare dividends, drawing the revolvers and collecting Ligado. Cash of USD 1,735.819 million covers the current portion 2.62 times, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress inside twelve months but not to repay the fiscal 2030 maturities without market access. Primary downside path: a slow ViaSat-3 ramp stalls EBITDA while interest stops being capitalized and the 2027 and fiscal 2030 maturities need refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Viasat presents an adequate business profile in aviation, government and defense, supported by recurring services, a USD 4,217.7 million firm backlog and USD 2,886.12 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by thin free cash flow, 4.49x leverage on unadjusted EBITDA and a concentrated maturity profile. Cash-flow durability appears weak because fiscal 2026 cash flow included one-off receipts. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on ViaSat-3 service starting on time, EBITDA growth and market access at costs near the 9.00% paid in 2024. A comparison with typical leveraged satellite and communications issuers is not established because no peer data was supplied. The primary downside path is a slow ViaSat-3 ramp feeding the 2027 and fiscal 2030 refinancing. Further analysis would require covenant levels, ratings and traded prices, an issuer adjusted EBITDA, the proxy statement and the cooperation agreement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: ViaSat-3 execution feeding refinancing of the fiscal 2030 maturities.
